metadata.title: doublevdesign - strategic design
metadata.description: Strategic design without the corporate fluff.

hero.description: People trust what they can see, feel, and experience. Authenticity isn't a marketing strategy - it's what makes a brand memorable. I create visual identities and design systems that give ideas a language people can connect with.

philosophy.heading: strategy you can actually feel.
philosophy.paragraphOne: Chances are: you're busy. You don't need more disconnected ideas, random visuals, or marketing that doesn't quite know where it's going. You need a clear direction and a brand that helps people understand what makes your business unique.
philosophy.paragraphTwo: Together, we turn ideas into a cohesive identity that feels authentic, works in the real world, and gives your brand something to grow into.

projects.heading: selected work
projects.intro: Design works best when it knows where it's going. These projects began by understanding the goal, then creating the clarity, systems, and visuals needed to move it forward.

items.title: Graz City Council election
items.overview: The campaign was working with a brand-new, Austria-wide corporate design that hadn't been tested in the field yet - and it was about to carry a major election campaign, with a team that hadn't worked together in this exact setup before. Responsibilities weren't always clearly split, so a lot of decisions about how the identity should actually work in practice landed with me. I took that on: building out the system across citylights, flyers, stickers, apparel, a cargo bike, a snack bar, and whatever else our team of creative minds came up with - including a set of custom trading cards, because why not.
items.more: Alongside the campaign team and an external designer, I produced the final visuals: traditional OOH-advertisements, Photoshop collage work, AI-supported illustration, and detailed mockups that guided both the photography and final production. A personal highlight: a before-and-after visualisation of a well-known city square, real vs. reimagined, that ran citywide - landing in every household's mailbox. The campaign ended up generating a solid amount of organic press coverage - a good sign the visual identity was landing the way it was meant to.

items.title: Auswendig Visual Identity
items.overview: The developer came to me with a great concept and name for his app, but wasn't sure yet what it should look like. After exploring a few rough drafts, we quickly landed on a visual identity – and once that clicked, the rest followed fast: who to target, where to advertise, how to talk about it in the Play Store listing and Google Ads. Out of that came a cohesive brand: logo, colour palette, light and dark theme variations, plus a set of custom icons to give the interface its own visual language. From there, I stayed involved in the finer details too: alignment, spacing, font sizing, flagging what needed adjusting as he built the interface, so the design held up in the actual product, not just on paper.
items.more: Beyond the identity, I helped bring Auswendig to life across its first public touchpoints. I designed the Google Play Store visuals and reviewed the German translation of the app to make sure it read naturally, shaping the tone and copywriting along the way. That same visual direction carried over to his website, where I helped pulling together assets, colours and typography into a cohesive personal brand.

items.title: Non-Profit Fundraising
items.overview: A children's crisis hotline needed a fundraising poster aimed at business donors - fast, on a tight budget, and without a full rebrand. The existing identity hadn't been touched in years, so the job was to work with what already existed rather than start from scratch.
items.more: After a few short calls to nail down what they needed, I put together two concepts based on their 2005 corporate design manual and an older campaign - headline, copy, and visuals included. They picked one, and we shaped it into a poster that reads as professional to a business audience while still feeling approachable - never pushy, never small, just direct. It's been in use ever since, with just a quick QR code swap and a small tweak a year in.

items.title: clim@ festival 2023-26
items.overview: The festival came with a solid brand identity and design manual from an external designer, but over three years and dozens of formats, most real-world use cases went beyond what the manual actually covered. On top of that, the people running the festival changed more than once - so alongside applying the identity myself across posters, flyers, print ads, merchandise, DOOH advertising, social content, and Google Ads, I became the point of reference for it: explaining the logic behind it to new organisers, designers, and social media people whenever they came on board, so the voice stayed consistent even as the team around it didn't.
items.more: Over those three years, I kept the brand aligned as both the applications and the people behind them kept changing - working closely with organisers, social media, and event planning to make sure new formats always felt like part of the same world, not one-off exceptions.
